summary: Ukrainian drones struck multiple Russian oil refineries and fuel infrastructure across Belgorod, Ulyanovsk, Bashkiria, and Crimea while Russian forces launched Oniks missiles at Odesa and threatened Iskander-M strikes from Crimea. The EU adopted its 21st sanctions package targeting 94 Russian banks, 37 long-range UAV producers, and 41 tankers. Zelensky appointed General-Major Ihor Skibiuk as new Chief of General Staff and signaled willingness to negotiate with Russia before autumn.
key_points: Ukrainian FPV drones destroyed gas stations in Belgorod region while long-range drones hit oil refineries in Ulyanovsk and Bashkiria and energy infrastructure in Yalta and occupied Luhansk. (Source: @eRadarrua/102261, @UkraineNow/82844)

Russian forces struck fuel unloading infrastructure in the port of Yuzhny and launched 1-2 Oniks missiles toward Odesa/Chornomorsk with additional missile preparations observed. (Source: @tass_agency/386727, @mon1tor_ua/69318, @mon1tor_ua/69311)

Massive waves of Shahed and reactive UAVs crossed from Chernihiv, Sumy, and Kyiv regions toward Zhytomyr, Kyiv, Poltava, and Bila Tserkva with Iskander-M threat from Crimea. EU 21st sanctions package targets 94 Russian banks, 33 financial organizations, 37 long-range UAV producers, 56 defense-linked entities, and 41 tankers bringing total to 673 vessels. (Source: @tass_agency/386718, @tass_agency/386715, @tass_agency/386711)

Zelensky appointed General-Major Ihor Skibiuk as Chief of General Staff; Fedorov declined deputy PM post seeking defense minister role; Ukraine seeks trilateral talks with US and Russia before autumn. (Source: @UkraineNow/82843, @ukr_leaks_eng/31846, @UkraineNow/82855)
Ukrainian drone destroyed Russian Buk-M3 air defense system worth $50M in Donetsk region; Su-57 fighter crashed near Moscow with pilot ejecting. (Source: @UkraineNow/82856, @UkraineNow/82852)

sections.executive_summary: Ukrainian long-range drones conducted coordinated strikes on Russian oil refineries in Ulyanovsk and Bashkiria, gas stations in Belgorod, and energy infrastructure in Yalta and occupied Luhansk, while a Ukrainian drone destroyed a Buk-M3 air defense system in Donetsk. Russian forces responded with Oniks missile strikes on Odesa port infrastructure, threatened Iskander-M launches from Crimea, and hit fuel unloading facilities in the port of Yuzhny. The EU imposed its 21st sanctions package targeting Russian banking, UAV production, and shadow tanker fleet as Zelensky appointed a new Chief of General Staff and pursued diplomatic engagement before autumn.

points: Ukrainian FPV drones continue systematic attacks on Belgorod region gas stations while long-range UAVs struck the Novospassky district oil refinery in Ulyanovsk region, the critical Subkhankulovo linear production dispatch station in Bashkiria, energy infrastructure in Yalta, and targets in occupied Luhansk overnight. (Source: @eRadarrua/102261, @UkraineNow/82844)

A Ukrainian drone successfully engaged and destroyed a Russian Buk-M3 air defense system valued at $50 million in Donetsk region on the night of July 23, exploiting the complex's forward repositioning near the front line. (Source: @UkraineNow/82856)

President Zelensky appointed General-Major Ihor Skibiuk as the new Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, while former Digital Transformation Minister Mykhailo Fedorov declined the deputy prime minister post for technological development, insisting on reinstatement as defense minister to implement army modernization. (Source: @UkraineNow/82843, @ukr_leaks_eng/31846)

Zelensky stated Ukraine wants to resume negotiations with Russia before autumn following a phone call with US envoys Kushner and Witkoff, proposing a trilateral meeting; he noted Russia is blocking the grain corridor and that cabinet changes were made months ago anticipating Russian winter plans. (Source: @UkraineNow/82855)

Fuel prices in Ukraine continue rising with A-95 gasoline reaching UAH 79.84 ($1.79) per liter and diesel UAH 83 ($1.85) per liter, adding economic pressure amid sustained Russian strikes on energy infrastructure. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31850)

Former Foreign Minister Dmytro Kuleba warned that 'all-out war is beginning' with both sides having sufficient missiles and drones to methodically destroy each other's economies, predicting very difficult times ahead and potential food shortages. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31856)

Russian forces struck fuel unloading infrastructure in the port of Yuzhny (Southern Ukraine) and launched 1-2 Oniks missiles toward Odesa/Chornomorsk with at least one additional missile preparing launch maneuvers toward the Moldavanka area. (Source: @tass_agency/386727, @mon1tor_ua/69318, @mon1tor_ua/69311)

A threat of Iskander-M ballistic missile launches from occupied Crimea was reported, while tactical aviation conducted launch maneuvers in Black Sea waters, indicating continued long-range strike preparation. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69316, @mon1tor_ua/69308)

Drone attacks on tankers near the KTK marine terminal may force Kazakhstan to adjust oil export and production plans, with Kazenergy calling for international coordination to protect civilian shipping. (Source: @tass_agency/386690)
A military aircraft, preliminarily identified as a modern Su-57 fighter by Russian publics, crashed near Moscow with the pilot ejecting; the cause remains undisclosed. (Source: @UkraineNow/82852)

Emergency regime declared in Nevinnomyssk (Stavropol Krai) where firefighters battle a blaze at a Wildberries warehouse following a UAV strike, according to the regional governor. (Source: @tass_agency/386724)

The SVR claimed the Ukrainian drone strike on the Sevastopol Defense Museum was a meticulously planned provocation by British intelligence, though details were not elaborated in the message. (Source: @tass_agency/386688)

Ukrainian drone destroyed a Russian Buk-M3 air defense system worth $50 million in Donetsk region on the night of July 23, catching occupiers off guard as they had moved the complex closer to the front line. (Source: @UkraineNow/82856)

Russian offensive efforts in Donbas continue to 'burn' through mobilized personnel with the analysis suggesting Moscow's 'cannon fodder' will be used to plug daily attrition gaps and attempt to reach regional borders rather than launch classic tank columns. (Source: @eRadarrua/102269)

Warfare has shifted 80% to the air domain with drones replacing classic infantry roles for reconnaissance, assault, position holding, and bunker clearing, making covert force accumulation near borders physically impossible. (Source: @eRadarrua/102269)

Russian tactics now emphasize massive drone swarms — nearly 5,000 UAVs in Sumy region last month plus guided aerial bombs — rather than ground offensives, with any concentrated troop formations vulnerable to destruction before reaching Ukrainian borders. (Source: @eRadarrua/102269)

Multiple reactive UAVs (Shahed-type) launched from Chernihiv region toward Hrabivka, Mena, Sorokoshchy, Bakhmach, Novgorod-Siverskyi, Ripky, and Kyiv region's Vyshhorod district and Kyiv Reservoir, with at least three Shaheds tracked toward Kyiv. (Source: @eRadarrua/102279, @eRadarrua/102290, @mon1tor_ua/69328, @kpszsu/69836)

Reactive UAVs from Kyiv region moved toward Zhytomyr region (Narodychi, past Malyn toward Cherniakhiv/Zhytomyr, and from north toward Zhytomyr) while Zhytomyr region saw three reactive UAVs toward Korosten and one past Malyn. (Source: @kpszsu/69840, @eRadarrua/102300, @kpszsu/69841, @eRadarrua/102298)

Sumy region reported a strike UAV toward Konotop and a new reactive UAV north of Chernihiv, while reactive UAVs from Chernihiv region headed toward Putyvl and Konotop in Sumy region. (Source: @eRadarrua/102287, @kpszsu/69822)
A reactive Shahed from the south headed toward Bila Tserkva (Kyiv region), and a 'Gerbera' UAV passed Bariшivka toward Obukhiv (Kyiv region). (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69331, @mon1tor_ua/69320)

sections.threat_assessment: The conflict is escalating into a full-spectrum air war with Ukraine demonstrating strategic reach by striking multiple Russian oil refineries and air defense systems deep inside Russia, while Russia responds with missile barrages on Ukrainian port infrastructure and ballistic missile threats from Crimea. The EU's 21st sanctions package targeting Russia's shadow tanker fleet and UAV production indicates long-term economic pressure, but Russian adaptation to drone-centric warfare — evidenced by massive Shahed waves across northern Ukraine and FPV saturation in Sumy — suggests continued high-intensity attrition. Zelensky's diplomatic overture for autumn talks coincides with personnel changes aimed at winter preparedness, yet Kuleba's warning of mutual economic destruction and rising fuel prices signal severe domestic strain. The destruction of a Buk-M3 and Su-57 crash highlight growing air defense vulnerabilities on both sides.
sections.regional_response: The EU's unified adoption of the 21st sanctions package after Greek objections were overcome demonstrates sustained transatlantic resolve to degrade Russian military-industrial capacity, particularly targeting long-range UAV producers and the shadow tanker fleet enabling oil revenue. Kazakhstan's alarm over tanker attacks near the KTK terminal reveals secondary economic risks to Central Asian energy exports, potentially drawing wider international coordination for Black Sea maritime security. Germany's explicit acknowledgment that the Bundeswehr must learn from Ukraine's combat experience signals a doctrinal shift in NATO's eastern flank defense planning. Meanwhile, Russia's SVR accusation of British involvement in the Sevastopol museum strike reflects ongoing information operations to frame Ukrainian strikes as Western provocations.
sections.intelligence_notes: The simultaneous reporting of reactive UAV tracks across Chernihiv, Sumy, Kyiv, Zhytomyr, and Poltava regions suggests a deliberate Russian saturation tactic to overwhelm air defenses and mask high-value missile launches (Oniks/Iskander-M). Ukraine's ability to strike the Subkhankulovo dispatch station — a critical Ural oil hub — and the Buk-M3 in Donetsk indicates improved ISR and targeting cycles for strategic assets. The Su-57 crash near Moscow, if confirmed, would represent a rare loss of Russia's most advanced fighter, potentially constraining its employment. Fedorov's insistence on the defense minister portfolio reveals internal friction over military reform priorities. The 5,000-drone monthly rate in Sumy alone quantifies the scale of Russia's drone-centric offensive, validating the assessment that warfare has shifted 80% to the air domain.
